name: Work Cut Off From Its Purpose
problem: Replies, experiments and finished work are chosen and judged from the quest alone, not from the top intent and metrics the quest serves, so effort can drift from what the person cares about most and gaps under an intent can go unnoticed.
who_has_it: Anyone with top intents above their quests, and maintainers iterating on a repository's solutions.
why_it_matters: The work done can differ from the work that matters, and the person is not told when an ideal has no solution, a solution has no quest or a metric has no data.
why_hard: The purpose lives in a specification that no prompt used to read, and adding it naively inflates every prompt and charges users who have no intents.
existing_attempts: Life intents specifications, written but read by little that does work; generic standing instructions in deep runs.

name: Answers Not Tied To The Person's Goal
problem: Asked how Quest could help, what a feature is for, or whether it is worth it, Quest AI can answer with a list of everything Quest has, or with a generic description, instead of the few features that fit this person's goal and circumstance, or it can assume a circumstance the person did not give.
who_has_it: People new to Quest, including visitors on the free plan, who describe a goal in a sentence and want to know what Quest would do for them.
why_it_matters: These questions help decide whether a person starts using Quest. A reply that leaves them to work out which features matter, or that describes a life they do not have, reads as a brochure and is easy to ignore.
why_hard: The fit needs the goal and circumstance from the message, the features from the documentation, and the judgment to leave out what does not help; a vague goal needs a question first, and a long list looks thorough, so padding is easy and is what a model often writes.
existing_attempts: A feature list written from the documentation, a guide page that lists the questions to ask back for a vague goal, and end-to-end cases that require the reply to name the person's own goal and circumstance and to invent no feature.
